newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds rose on Wednesday for the second consecutive day as investors' interest flagged in inflation-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.08 pct to 103.95
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: unchanged at 103.12
Volume was a low 100 million shekels.
"The market is very stable now. CPI-linked bonds reached a new equilibrium following their recent rise and investors prefer to invest in unlinked bonds," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.

"CPI-linked bonds closed unchanged today with short bonds rising and long bonds falling. These bonds made a big move and now they are less attractive," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.

"Because of the rise of the inflation-linked bonds, unlinked bonds became more attractive. They offer yields of 13.8 percent which is very attractive considering the fact that the 1997 inflation is expected to be around 8.2 percent," the Hapoalim trader said.
Makams closed unchanged on low volume of only 32 million shekels.

Dollar-linked bonds were today's main losers after the shekel rose mildly against the dollar. In the local market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3650 shekels against 3.3670 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
